issue: 'Place Order' CTA is gray on gray and 12px — nearly invisible

iterations.final_answer: Users scan for the most visually actionable element and execute it. High contrast fill with a readable label = 'this is available, this is the action.' Low contrast, small label = 'this is disabled, skip it.' Those signals are automatic — users don't reason through them. The primary CTA on a checkout screen needs to send the right signal. 'Place Order' is sending the disabled signal. The design is making the one element that has to be executed look like the one element that should be skipped.

Solid fill: brand color, white label text — standard primary button. WCAG AA: 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum for the 14–16px label. 3:1 minimum for the button boundary against background. Current gray on gray fails both. One CSS change: background-color, color, font-size. Three properties. Done.

Label at ≥14–16px. Primary CTA needs to read as the most actionable element on the screen. Right now it reads as the least actionable. That's the root and the fix.
